data.reasoning: Two independent models (qwen3-235b and deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD and found it safe. The package follows standard AUR patterns: fetches a pinned GitHub release tarball (v2.3.11) with SHA-256 checksum verification, and performs standard file installation in the package() function. No top-level code execution, no dynamic downloads, no suspicious constructs. The inconclusive verdicts were caused by tool errors (HTTP 400 API failure for .SRCINFO in qwen, parse error in openrouter/free), not security concerns. The openrouter/free report is marked advisory:true and doesn't count as a vote. All successful file reviews found no injection patterns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failures, not security findings. qwen3-235b had an HTTP 400 error when reviewing .SRCINFO, and openrouter/free had a parse error when reviewing PKGBUILD. Both models successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD (qwen) or .SRCINFO (openrouter) and found them safe. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed both files and found them safe. No model found any actual security issues.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: .SRCINFO review failed due to HTTP 400 API error
openrouter/free: PKGBUILD review failed due to parse error (model returned non-standard format)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parse errors) should not contribute to the final verdict - they should be excluded from the agreement calculation and clearly marked as coverage gaps rather than inconclusive security findings

When a model successfully reviews the PKGBUILD (the primary attack surface) and finds it safe, and the .SRCINFO review fails due to a tool error, the verdict should lean toward safe rather than inconclusive
The openrouter/free model's parse error suggests the need for more robust output format enforcement or fallback parsing for free-tier models that may not follow structured output requirements
